paras: The shooting of Will Wilkerson took place at Malvern, Arkansas, on or about June 19, 1881, when a town marshal named Hall dangerously wounded Wilkerson, a Black man, while trying to arrest him. Wilkerson escaped to the woods and was still at large when the news was telegraphed from Little Rock the next day, with a number of people pursuing him.

According to the dispatch, Wilkerson was wanted on the accusation that, about a year earlier, he had shot and killed Charles Brunek, the postmaster at Galloway, in a quarrel about a post-office money order.

Wilkerson was "discovered in Malvern" on the day before the dispatch, and an attempt was made to arrest him. In the attempt he was "dangerously wounded by Marshal Hall," but he got away into the woods. The report gives no details of the confrontation, such as whether Wilkerson was armed or who fired first.
At the time of the dispatch Wilkerson was "still at large," and "a number of persons" were pursuing him. No report of his capture, death or trial appears in the coverage found.

The episode is known from a single paragraph dated Little Rock, June 20, printed on June 21 in the Chicago Daily Tribune among a column of short crime dispatches from around the country. The item called Wilkerson "a colored desperado" and stated the killing of the postmaster as fact rather than as a charge. No other account, including any from an Arkansas paper, was found.
